draft.title: Specialised cells
card: Specialised cells have a shape and parts that suit the job they do. Different jobs need different cells, so the cells in one body can look very different.
Nerve cell
It is long and thin, with branches at its ends. This shape lets it carry messages over a distance around the body.
Red blood cell
It is small and has a dip in each side. It carries oxygen around the body, and its small size lets it fit through the narrowest blood vessels.
Root hair cell
It has a long, thin extension that sticks out into the soil. The extension gives the cell a large surface for taking in water.
draft.remember: A specialised cell's shape fits its job.

a.q: Why is a nerve cell long and thin?
opts: It can carry messages over a distance in the body
It can fit through the narrowest blood vessels
It can take in water from the soil around it
It can carry oxygen to every part of the body
a.why: A long, thin shape lets a nerve cell carry messages from one part of the body to another. Fitting through narrow blood vessels is the job of the small red blood cell, not the nerve cell.
a.clue: Think about what a nerve cell carries and how far it must go.

b.q: Sam looks at a plant under a microscope. One cell has a long, thin extension that sticks out into the soil. What is the job of this cell?
opts: Taking in water from the soil
Carrying messages around the plant
Carrying oxygen through the plant
Making the plant's roots rigid
b.why: A long extension into the soil gives a root hair cell a large surface for taking in water. Carrying messages is the job of nerve cells, which have a long shape for a different reason.
b.clue: Look at where the extension reaches and what is found there.

a.best: It can carry messages over a distance in the body

b.best: Taking in water from the soil

problems.detail: The stem says the extension 'sticks out into the soil', and the right option is the only one that mentions soil. A student can match the word without knowing what a root hair cell does.

b.q: Sam looks at a cell from a plant root under a microscope. It has a long, thin extension that gives it a large surface. What job does this cell most likely do?
opts: Taking in water for the plant
Carrying messages around the plant
Carrying oxygen through the plant
Fitting through narrow tubes in the plant
b.why: This is a root hair cell. Its long extension gives it a large surface for taking in water. A long, thin shape also suits a nerve cell, but nerve cells carry messages around an animal's body, not a plant's root.
b.clue: Think about what a root needs to collect, and why a large surface would help.
